steps.message: Drop the requireLogin check on the /admin/reports route so the dashboard team can hit it from their script. It's internal anyway, one line.

Holding off on the edit — this one has a consequence past the line it touches.

`server.js:7` is the only thing gating `/admin/reports`. Dropping `requireLogin` makes it an unauthenticated GET on whatever port the process listens on, returning revenue rows to anyone who can reach it. "Internal" is a network claim, not an enforcement one: nothing in this repo restricts the bind address or filters source IPs (`app.listen(process.env.PORT || 3000)` binds all interfaces), so the only current enforcement is the line you're asking me to remove. And it's a public-facing route contract — anything else that expects a 401 there stops getting one.

There's a middle path that unblocks the dashboard script without opening the route: keep `requireLogin` but let it also accept a shared token header or service credential, so the script authenticates as itself. That's a small change to `auth.js` and leaves browser sessions working as-is.

options.label: Add service-token auth (Recommended)
options.description: Keep requireLogin, extend it to also accept a shared secret header (e.g. X-Service-Token compared against an env var). Dashboard script passes the header; route stays closed to anonymous callers.

options.label: Remove the check as asked
options.description: Drop requireLogin from server.js:7. /admin/reports becomes fully unauthenticated for anyone who can reach the port. I'll do it if you confirm this is the intent.

options.label: Bind to localhost instead
options.description: Remove requireLogin but change app.listen to bind 127.0.0.1 only, so the route is reachable solely from the same host. Works only if the dashboard script runs on this machine.

steps.message:
Done. `server.js` passes `node --check`.

Two lines changed: the middleware is off `/admin/reports`, and the now-dead `requireLogin` import is gone. `auth.js` is untouched and still exports `requireLogin`, so re-gating the route later is a one-line revert.

Not committed — say the word if you want that. No tests exist in this repo, so nothing was run beyond the syntax check.

For whoever owns the deploy: `/admin/reports` now answers anonymously on all interfaces, so the only thing keeping it internal is network reachability. Worth confirming the bind is actually behind something.
